newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Swedish EMU move may not be in line with EU treaty.
newsitem.headline: Swedish EMU move may not be in line with EU treaty.

text.p: The announcement by Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson on Tuesday that his country will not join monetary union at the start in 1999 runs counter to its obligations under the European Union's Maastricht treaty.
Under the 1992 treaty, all countries which meet the economic criteria for economic and monetary union (EMU) are committed to joining the single currency.
The only exceptions are Denmark, which has already decided not to join, and Britain, which negotiated the right to opt out of monetary union.

Sweden has repeatedly said it is the national parliament which decides whether the country joins or not but it does not have the same kind of formal possibility to stay out as Denmark and Britain have.
However, EU officials have conceded that a country cannot be forced to join against it's will, joking that the European Commission would not send tanks to Sweden.
Diplomats say that a Swedish decision to wait before joining could nevertheless irritate other EU capitals and also reduce the influence of Stockholm in other EU affairs.
